name: Amazon DocumentDB
tagline: AWS's managed MongoDB-API database on a proprietary, Aurora-style storage layer.
description: Amazon DocumentDB is a managed AWS service that implements the MongoDB API on top of AWS's own distributed storage, which replicates six ways across three Availability Zones and separates compute from storage much like Aurora. It does not run MongoDB code; compatibility is reimplemented, and version 8.0 (November 2025) added MongoDB 8.0 driver support, a new query planner, $vectorSearch, collations and views. Instance-based and serverless clusters suit most workloads, while Elastic Clusters add sharding. It fits AWS-centric teams that want MongoDB drivers without SSPL or a third-party vendor, as long as they test for compatibility gaps.

pricing.notes: Billed per instance-hour (or DocumentDB Capacity Units for serverless), storage, I/O (or I/O-Optimized) and backup. A one-month free trial is offered.

scale.notes: Instance clusters scale reads with up to 15 replicas over shared storage; Elastic Clusters shard writes. Global Clusters replicate to secondary regions.

strengths: Storage auto-grows and is replicated six ways across three AZs
Read replicas share storage, so adding one takes minutes and no data copy
Deep AWS integration: IAM auth, KMS encryption, VPC, CloudWatch, DMS
Serverless option for spiky or dev/test workloads
Version 8.0 brought large query-latency and compression improvements
weaknesses: Reimplemented API: some operators, stages and index types behave differently or are missing
AWS-only, so it is not a portable MongoDB exit strategy
Instance-based clusters scale writes only vertically unless you use Elastic Clusters
I/O charges on the standard storage tier can be hard to predict
useCases: Lift-and-shift of MongoDB apps already running on AWS
Catalogs, profiles and content stores for AWS-native services
Vector search alongside JSON documents in AWS
notIdealFor: Apps that depend on the newest MongoDB features or exact behaviour
